8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  8A.  Conditional Use Permit 15-035 Time Extension No. 1 and Site Plan
  Review 18-007 Time Extension No. 1
  Le Nguyen, Applicant

  A request for a two-year time extension to construct five buildings totaling
  approximately 18,000 square feet in two phases for a religious assembly
  use located at 3347 East Avenue S.

  Assistant Planner Jasmine Alvarado presented this item and directed the
  Planning Commission to the memorandum with the following amendment
  to the Resolution:

  3  The Planning Commission hereby finds as follows with respect to the
  environmental document prepared in connection with SPR 18-007
  TE No. 1 and CUP 15-035 TE No. 1:

  (a)  SPR 18-007 TE No. 1 and Conditional Use Permit 15-035 TE
  No. 1 are exempt from the requirements of the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and CEQA Guidelines.
  The project has been previously reviewed under CEQA and
  determined to be Categorically Exempt pursuant to Section
  15332, Class 32, of the CEQA Guidelines. The previously
  approved project has not changed and the proposed TE’s
  merely involves a request for a two-year time extension to
  inaugurate the entitlements. Therefore, the proposed TE will
  not have a significant effect on the environment.

  Chair Nemeth asked for clarification on Condition Nos. 1 and 2 with
  regarding to the inauguration of the project and possibly making Condition
  No. 2 less harsh and restrictive. Planning Manager Taggart stated that
  these Conditions were carried over from the initial approval and staff can
 Planning Commission Minutes
August 12, 2021
Page 3

  certainly add any recommendation that the Commission would desire.
  Below is the amendment to Condition No. 2 per the Commission’s request:

  2  This approval shall not become effective for any purposes until any
  appeal period has passed, the applicant has filed at the office of the
  Planning Division their notarized affidavit stating that they agree to,
  and accept, all of the Conditions of Approval as approved by the
  reviewing authority as set forth in Exhibit V to RESOLUTION NO.
  PC-2021-019.  The Site Plan Review shall be considered
  inaugurated if applicable building permits have been issued and
  above-ground construction has been initiated and is on-going.
  Cessation of construction for more than 180 days shall result in a
  lapse of this Site Plan Review. (P)

  Chair Nemeth opened the public hearing.

  Mr. Paul Swearingen, the applicant’s representative, agreed with the
  amended language to Condition No. 2. Mr. Swearingen also noted that they
  are ready to start construction immediately.

  Chair Nemeth closed the public hearing on this item. No objection; so
  ordered.

  Motion: Adopt RESOLUTION NO. PC-2021-019, as amended by the
  memorandum and the Planning Manager’s amended wording of Condition
  No. 2, approving Conditional Use Permit 15-035 Time Extension No. 1 and
  Site Plan Review 18-007 Time Extension No. 1 and find that the project is
  Categorically Exempt from environmental review.

  Motion was made by Commissioner Fraga-Saenz and seconded by
  Commissioner Smith.

  Vote:  Motion carried 4-0-0-1
  Yes:  Chair Nemeth; Commissioners Fraga-Saenz, Henderson, and

  8C.  Site Plan Review 20-012 and Density Bonus Agreement 20-001
  Highridge Costa Development Company, Applicant

  A request to construct an affordable multiple-family residential development
  located on the northeast corner of East Avenue R and 30th Street East
  (APN: 3020-005-031).

  Associate Planner Justin Sauder presented this item and directed the
  Planning Commission to the memorandum with the following amendments
  to the Resolution:
 Planning Commission Minutes
August 12, 2021
Page 5

  THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS SHALL BE ADDRESSED WITH THE
  SUBMITTAL OF GRADING PLANS OR PRIOR TO ISSUANCE OF A
  GRADING PERMIT:

  44  An updated botanical survey utilizing Manual of California Vegetation
  (MCV)-defined alliances shall be conducted. Based on the Protocols
  for Surveying and Evaluating Impacts to Special Status Native Plant
  Populations and Sensitive Natural Communities (CDFW, 2018), a
  qualified biologist shall conduct botanical surveys in the field at the
  times of year when plants will be both evident and identifiable. (P)

  45  The Project applicant shall actively implement Best Management
  Practices (BMPs) to prevent potential erosion and the discharge of
  sediment and/or pollutants into adjacent riparian areas during Project
  grading activities. BMPs shall be monitored and repaired, if
  necessary, to ensure maximum erosion, sediment, and pollution
  control. The Project applicant shall prohibit the use of erosion control
  materials potentially harmful to fish and wildlife species, such as
  mono-filament netting (erosion control matting) or similar material.
  All fiber rolls, straw wattles, and/or hay bales utilized within and
  adjacent to the Project site shall be free of nonnative plant materials.
  Fiber rolls or erosion control mesh shall be made of loose-weave
  mesh that is not fused at the intersections of the weave, such as jute,
  or coconut (coir) fiber, or other products without welded weaves. (P)

  THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS SHALL BE COMPLETED PRIOR TO
  OR IN CONJUNCTION WITH ISSUANCE OF BUILDING PERMITS:

  78  Special status species information shall be submitted to the
  California Natural Diversity Database (CNDDB) by completing the
  Online Field Survey Form (CDFW 2021c) and confirmation of data
  submitted shall be provided to CDFW. (P)

  THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS SHALL  BE  MET  WHILE
  CONSTRUCTION ACTIVITIES ARE ON-GOING:

  94  All hollow posts and pipes shall be capped to prevent wildlife
  entrapment and mortality. Metal fence stakes used on the Project
  site shall be plugged with bolts or other plugging materials to avoid
  this hazard. (P)
 Planning Commission Minutes
August 12, 2021
Page 6

  In addition, there are also minor edits to the mitigation measures for the
  project that will be outlined within the Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting
  Program (MMRP) along with the FINAL Conditions of Approval.

  The Planning Commission had no technical questions for staff.

  Chair Nemeth opened the public hearing.

  One eComment was received in opposition of the project from
  Ramona Aloyo.

  Chair Nemeth stated that Abundant Housing LA sent an email to the
  Commission regarding this project.

  Mr. Richard Fleishman spoke in opposition of this project.

  Mr. William Gates spoke in opposition of this project.

  Mr. Darryl Foster spoke in opposition of this project. Mr. Foster is concerned
  with the dust and traffic that will generated.

  Ms. Monica Slone spoke in opposition of this project.

  Mr. Jose Arellano spoke in opposition of this project.

  Ms. Freida Green spoke in opposition of this project.

  Ms. Karmisha Myvett spoke in opposition of this project.

  Ms. Ramona Aloyo spoke again in opposition of this project. Ms. Aloyo also
  submitted an eComment.

  Ms. Martha Kauffman spoke in opposition of this project.

  Ms. Della Acosta spoke in opposition of this project.

  Mr. Juda Toledano spoke in opposition of this project.

  Mr. Juan Carrillo spoke in favor of this project.
 Planning Commission Minutes
August 12, 2021
Page 7

  Chair Nemeth closed the public hearing on this item. No objection; so
  ordered.

  Commissioner Henderson asked staff if there are any requirements for dust
  control. Associate Planner Sauder stated that the applicant is conditioned
  to provide a dust control plan to the Antelope Valley Air Quality
  Management District per Condition No. 26.

  Mr. Mohammad Mohana with Highridge Costa Development Company
  stated that they have specific requirements for dust control. Mr. Mohana
  stated that they looked throughout Palmdale for their site which begins with
  a willing landowner wanting to sell then all the other parameters come in to
  play of where we develop. Mr. Mohana explained how the individuals are
  vetted to be able to live in this community. Mr. Mohana added that security
  will be provided at this site for the residents.

  Ms. Vicky Razo, Senior Housing Coordinator with the City of Palmdale,
  works specifically on Density Bonus Agreements and confirms compliance
  with these agreements. There is also a management plan that needs to be
  submitted by the developer 180 days prior to occupancy of any
  development. Senior Housing Coordinator Razo assures the services that
  are needed are provided. In addition, all new developments are required to
  be part of our Partners Against Crime program.

  Chair Nemeth stated that these residents are concerned about their safety
  because of McAdam Park and the 7-Eleven at the northwest corner of
  Avenue R and 30th Street East. Chair Nemeth also added that the City has
  Regional Housing numbers that we have to reach and have available
  housing at all economic levels.

  Motion:  Adopt RESOLUTION NO. PC-2021-022, as amended,
  recommending City Council approval of Density Bonus Agreement 20-001
  (A-7437), approving Site Plan Review 20-012 and adopting the Mitigated
  Negative Declaration and Mitigation Monitoring Reporting Program
  prepared for the project.

  Motion was made by  Chair  Nemeth  and  seconded  by
  Commissioner Fraga-Saenz.

TO:  Members of the Planning Commission

FROM:  Megan Taggart, Planning Manager

PREPARED BY:  Justin Sauder, Associate Planner

SUBJECT:  Agenda Item 8A; Zoning Ordinance Amendment 21-003

DATE:  September 2, 2021

The item is being continued until the October 14, 2021, Planning Commission meeting to
allow staff to incorporate additional changes to the amendment.
   C.P.T.E.D.
Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design
  City of Palmdale Public Safety
 FOUR ELEMENTS OF CPTED
• NATURAL SURVEILLANCE
• ACCESS CONTROL
• TERRITORIAL REINFORCEMENT
• MAINTENANCE
 Element 1 – Natural Surveillance:

• Natural Surveillance- Naturally occurring. As people are moving
  around an area, they will be able to observe the activity around
  them.
  • Trim large trees and shrubs to ensure no tree branches are
  below six feet and no shrubs are above two feet to prevent
  hiding places.
  • Install see-through fencing wherever possible.
  • Use barrier plants to discourage access and climbing.
  • Sufficient lighting
 Element 1- Natural Surveillance
 Element 1- Natural Surveillance
 Element 2- Access Control

• Access Control- The physical guidance of people coming and going
  from a space by the judicial placement of entrances, fences,
  landscaping, and lighting.
  • Clearly define entrances and exits
  • Security fencing, gates, and hostile vegetation
 Element 2- Access Control
 Element 3- Territorial Reinforcement

• Creates a clear delineation of space that separates your space
  from non-legitimate users.
  • Features that define property lines and distinguish private
  spaces from public spaces, such as landscape plantings,
  pavement design, gateway treatments, and fences.
 Element 3- Territorial Reinforcement
 Element 4- Maintenance

• A well-maintained area sends the message that people notice and
  care about what happens in an area. This, in turn, discourages
  vandalism and other crimes. Security practitioners refer to the
  "Broken Windows Theory," the idea that one broken window will
  entice vandals to break another. A vandalized area then becomes
  more inviting to higher levels of crime. A property should be well-
  maintained as a matter of safety as well as pride.
 Element 4- Maintenance
